exposure: Prenatally detected small for gestational age (SGA)
cohort: 718 singleton infants born SGA in cephalic position between 36 and 41 weeks gestation
finding: While there was no significant difference in composite adverse neonatal outcomes between prenatally detected and non-prenatally detected SGA infants born at term, prenatal detection was associated with higher rates of labor induction and cesarean sections, potentially contributing to the observed absence of perinatal mortality in the prenatally detected group.
mod_finding: Prenatal detection of SGA was associated with higher rates of cesarean sections.
